No environment variable value is printed anywhere in this record.

### ① Derived judgments

The card's six change items, the five pinned cases, the marker test and the PR's claims, one at a time:

1. File surface. Five commits (d031f75a, 80392c96, b01f92ae, 1bae3e40, d2ee86ca; commit author Claude; PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`). `git diff 28d0dbbf d2ee86ca --stat`, the REST file listing and `changed_files: 7` agree on exactly: rest-channel.md +1/−0, security-findings.md +1/−0, check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs +10/−2, dispatch.mjs +356/−21, execute.mjs +239/−5, ops.mjs +368/−16, validate.mjs +196/−23 (1,171/67, under the 3,000 human-merge line). The blobs at head are the four the PR body names (ops 7d2ba294, validate 8ea5abcd, execute 9c70c7cd, dispatch 51075987). No NUL byte in any of the seven. The claim's file surface is exactly these seven; `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` is untouched, as the claim required. On surface.
2. The row and the grant, least privilege. `OPS.advisory_read` is `permission: 'repository-advisories'`, `grant: 'read'`, `senderGate: 'collaborator'`, `required: ['ghsa_id', 'public_key']`, `optional: []`, `alone: true`, one request: a GET of one advisory's path carrying an `advisoryRead` descriptor. `tokenPermissionsOf` now carries a level per stroke-scoped permission (`levelOf` = the row's `grant`, else `PERMISSIONS`' level; write wins when two rows meet, which `alone` makes unreachable), so a read stroke's `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` line is `permission_repository_advisories=read` and `permission_actions=` is empty; every other advisory stroke still mints write; every non-advisory stroke still writes an empty value. The validator's self-test pins all of that through the real process (the `cliRuns[0].output` case), and the grant ledger case pins that `advisory_read` is the only row naming a `grant`, on a stroke-scoped permission, never above the table's level. The `strokeErrors` text changed from a hard-coded `write` to the row's grant, which for every existing row is the same string. The dev's A6 (read raised to write) and A10 (`alone` removed) were not re-run here; they are not leak paths and the row pin covers both. Correct.
3. The `public_key` field, validated strictly and never echoed. `advisoryReadKeyFailure`: a string, exactly 60 characters, the X25519 SPKI prefix pinned by `ADVISORY_READ_PUBLIC_KEY_SHAPE` with the canonical pad character set (the last group's spare bits clear, so one spelling), parsed as SPKI DER, `asymmetricKeyType === 'x25519'`, then a trial derivation against a fresh private key with an all-zero or thrown result refused as a low-order point; every reason is a fixed sentence. The validator's refusal is `must be one X25519 public key, base64 SPKI DER of exactly 60 characters — got <describeQuietly(value)> that <why>`, and `describeQuietly` is type and byte count alone. Measured: the validator's battery refuses 29 malformed shapes (non-strings, short, long, unpadded, padded with a space, base64url alphabet, a spare bit set, Ed25519, X448, PEM, raw key in two encodings, DER in hex, the seven low-order points of the curve) and the echo sweep finds no 16-character run of any of them in any refusal. Ablation A4 (the refusal prints `JSON.stringify(value)`) reds 1 of 303 (the no-echo case); A4b reds 2 of 253 (the marker test and the real-process case). Correct.
4. The crypto. `sealAdvisoryRead`: a fresh X25519 pair per seal (`generateKeyPairSync` inside the function), `diffieHellman` with the recipient, HKDF-SHA256 with an empty salt and an info of the scheme label plus both raw public keys (empty salt is RFC 5869's optional form and the info binds the two parties, which is the right thing to bind), a 32-byte AES-256-GCM key, a random 12-byte nonce, a 16-byte tag, `setAAD(aad)` with `advisoryReadAad` = label, request id, action index and advisory id; the envelope is one version byte ‖ ephemeral raw key ‖ nonce ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag in unpadded base64url (61 bytes of overhead, pinned); the shared secret and the AES key are zeroed in `finally`; an all-zero secret throws before any key is derived. `openAdvisoryRead` refuses non-canonical base64url, a short box, another version, and any decryption failure with one fixed sentence; it decodes with a fatal UTF-8 decoder; it never exports the private key (`diffieHellman({ privateKey })` and `createPublicKey(privateKey)` read the `KeyObject`). The reviewer's independent decrypt from the header's description alone opens a sealed envelope to the exact plaintext, finds a different ephemeral key and nonce on a second seal of the same text, finds no marker in the sealed characters or decoded bytes, and fails under a different AAD — so the documented format is the implemented one. Failures never fall back: a thrown seal and a seal that returns the plaintext are each a FAILED action with `ADVISORY_READ_SEAL_FAILED`, zero parts, and the exception's message printed nowhere; a result that is not a base64url string is the same FAILED. Ablations: A8 (a thrown seal falls back to the plaintext as base64url) reds 1 of 253; R2 (the exception's message becomes the row's reason) reds 2 of 253 including the marker test; R5 (AAD dropped from seal and open together) reds the "opens for its own read alone" case in validate (1 of 303) and in execute (1 of 253), each on the other-action and other-advisory arms exactly. The key pair is one-time: `armAdvisoryReads` makes one per read action per process, keeps the private half in a `Map` local to `main`, and the dispatch self-test reads its own source to pin that no `privateKey.export(` exists above the self-test, the file's one `node:fs` import is `readFileSync`, and no module-level key map exists. Sound.
5. The leak surface, read against the code rather than the tests. On the read path the executor's row is `{ call: advisoryReadCall(repo), status, result }` where the call is the path with `{ghsa_id}` left in as a placeholder, `result` is `advisoryReadLandedText` (three counts) or `FAILED: <why>`; `why` is the fence text (fixed sentences; the sender fence prints the dispatcher's login through `advisoryPrintable` with the login shape, never an answered value; the advisory fence says "names another advisory", never which), plus `advisoryPlatformText(detail)` which prints the platform's `message` only when `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES` lists it, plus `ADVISORY_READ_ACCESS_REMEDY`; or `ADVISORY_READ_SEAL_FAILED`; or `advisoryReadOverCapText` (two counts). The log line is `✓/✗ action i op: <call> -> HTTP s · <result>`, the step summary's table prints call, status and result, `stoppedAt.why` is the same `why`, and the only other emission is `::notice title=fleet-write advisory_read::fleet-write action=i op=advisory_read part=k/n sealed=<chunk>` per part. `detail` on a `status: 0` transport failure is the fetch error's text, which the allow-list does not print. No path prints the id, the state, the summary, the description, a vulnerability or any other answered field. Measured: the marker sweep covers 18 executor runs (landed, long, both gates and the unknown gate, the read, advisory and sender fences, a thrown seal, an unsealed seal, over cap, seven refused payloads) plus four real processes, and finds the marker and both ids on no log line, row, summary, annotation, pace-log line, stdout, stderr, `GITHUB_OUTPUT` or step summary, with the opened text as the positive control. Ablations: A2 (the landed row appends the answer's summary) reds 2 of 253 (the landed row, the marker test); A3 (the row prints the real path) reds 3 (the landed row, the fence rows, the id sweep); R1 (the sealed branch made unreachable, so the GET falls through the generic row printer) reds 12 of 253 including the marker test and the id sweep, which is the whole point of the branch; R4 (the advisory fence names the answered id) reds 1 of 303 and R4b reds 2 of 253 (the fence rows, the id sweep). Holds on every path this review could reach.
6. The sender gate, enforced in the runner and out of the payload's reach. The executor's existing target-write gate (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{login}/permission`) runs before any action on every stroke; the read then judges `ADVISORY_READ_FENCES` with `sender` from `FLEET_WRITE_SENDER`, which the workflow sets to `github.event.sender.login` (read, outside the surface), and `gate` from `OPS.advisory_read.senderGate`, a default parameter on a frozen table; the only override is `deps.advisoryRead`, which `main()` never passes (it passes `{ log }` alone), and the validator refuses any key on the action other than `ghsa_id` and `public_key` by name (`senderGate`, `sender`, `private_key`, `reveal` and the answer's field names among the pinned refusals). `collaborator` requires the sender's login, compared case-insensitively, in the advisory's own `collaborating_users`; teams are deliberately not read; `target-write` returns null (the first gate already held); any other value, including empty or absent, fails closed. Ablation A5 (the collaborator gate opened without reading the list) reds 1 of 253 (the stranger with write on the target); A5b reds 3 of 303 (the sender fence, the read-fence ordering, the fence sentence). Enforced.
7. Chunking and reassembly, correct and capped. `advisoryReadParts` cuts the sealed text into 4,000-character parts, at most 10, returning null for empty or over 40,000 characters; 40,000 base64url characters is 30,000 envelope bytes, less 61 of overhead, so 29,939 plaintext bytes — the validator's `largest`/`overOne` case seals exactly 29,939 and 29,940 bytes and gets 10 parts and null. Each notice message is `prefix action=i op=op part=k/n sealed=<chunk>` under the runner's 4,096-character cut (pinned at the longest chunk). The parser is anchored, accepts only `ADVISORY_READ_OPS` (derived from the table as the rows requiring `public_key`, so exactly one today), `1 ≤ part ≤ of ≤ 10`, a base64url chunk of 1 to 4,000 characters, nothing trailing. `assembleAdvisoryReads` requires one `of` per action, every part 1..n present, a repeated part identical, and two texts under one number a refusal; it never picks between answers. An over-cap answer is a FAILED action with counts alone and zero parts (pinned). The dispatch's end-to-end case runs the real executor, turns its notice lines into annotations, and opens them byte for byte; six unverified shapes (no key in this process, no part, a missing part, a tampered part, parts sealed to another seat's key, unreadable annotations) are each `unverified`, exit 6, `plaintext: null`, nothing printed. Correct.
8. The seat side, `--reveal` as the one door. `main()` arms the keys before packing; a `public_key` already in the actions file is refused (exit 2) with a sentence that never echoes it; `--reveal` on a stroke with no read is exit 2 before anything is sent; after `sendFleetWrite` the opened text is written with `console.log` to stdout only inside `if (opts.reveal)`; `advisoryReadLine` on stderr carries counts and the top-level field names of the opened JSON; `--json`'s `advisory_reads` carries state, bytes, fields, parts and why, never text; `unverifiedText` reads `readBack` and `runs` rows only. The proxy re-exec child inherits stdio and arms its own pair from the actions file, so the plaintext still lands only on the seat's own stdout. Ablations: A7 (the text printed without `--reveal`) reds 1 of 315; R3 (`--json` carries the text) reds 2 of 315. Correct.

Base vs head, both measured here: validate 275/15 → 303/16 (+28, one battery), execute 237/21 → 253/22 (+16, one battery), dispatch 298/26 → 315/27 (+17, one battery); each file's battery floor rose by one; `rerun-failed` 31/5 unchanged.
